A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Simple Policy Optimization. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and additional material in v5.

before.justification: v2 reports original Atari experiments measuring returns, KL divergence, and policy entropy, including over-optimization, network-depth, and threshold-sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains original Atari results and adds experiments on six MuJoCo continuous-control tasks, with learning curves and numerical return comparisons.

M1.justification: The SPO objective, advantage-sign adjustment, and update sequence remain unchanged. Section 4.4 adds a continuous-action adaptation using independent Gaussian policy components and their closed-form KL divergences, extending the categorical-action formulation documented in v2.

E1.justification: v5 adds continuous-control evaluation on Ant, HalfCheetah, Hopper, Humanoid, HumanoidStandup, and Walker2d in MuJoCo, substantially extending the action-space and task coverage beyond Atari. The 35-game Atari coverage remains; adding '-v5' to plot titles does not establish different Atari tasks.

E2.justification: PPO-Clip, PPO-Penalty, and PPO with early stopping remain in the Atari comparisons. Removing v2 Figure 1 also removes its directly optimized surrogate-objective comparator, SO. The new MuJoCo experiments compare against the already represented PPO-Clip method rather than introducing a new baseline family.

E3.justification: The retained Atari preprocessing and hyperparameter table are unchanged. v5 introduces a separate MuJoCo protocol with horizon 256, 10 update epochs, learning rate 0.0003, and budgets of 3 million or 10 million steps. Tables 1–2 additionally evaluate returns over the final 10% and the entire training process.

E4.justification: v5 adds MuJoCo comparisons across KL thresholds and KL-divergence/entropy diagnostics in Figure 13. It removes the 100-epoch Amidar demonstration and Riverraid from the 1,000-epoch stress test. Existing Atari network-depth and threshold-sensitivity analyses remain, largely relocated into Appendices B.5 and B.7.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations across three seeds for Atari. v5 specifies five seeds with standard-deviation reporting for MuJoCo; this is new experiment-specific information, not an increase in retained Atari runs. The five-seed disclosure accompanying the removed Amidar demonstration also disappears.

E6.justification: v5 adds substantial MuJoCo results absent from v2. Table 1 reports final-window returns of 3168.32 versus 822.57 for SPO-0.03 versus PPO on Humanoid, but 4628.01 versus 5216.36 on Ant. Table 2 adds whole-training averages showing further tradeoffs. Amidar and Riverraid stress-test results are removed; these changes do not establish before-and-after performance gains.

T1.justification: v5 changes the TRPO theorem and corollary coefficient from 2 to 4, expands the policy-gradient derivation, and derives an improvement inequality using the lower bound M. It also introduces Gaussian-policy assumptions and proves the Gaussian KL formula in Appendix B.6. These are bounded mathematical additions and revisions; no new SPO convergence theorem is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets, and Discussion retain the same central claims: KL clipping, better Atari sample efficiency, low KL divergence, higher entropy, robustness to network depth, and first-order simplicity. The continuous-control experiments do not materially rewrite these core contribution statements.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds interpretation of the MuJoCo results: it attributes Humanoid gains tentatively to excessive PPO KL divergence and distinguishes final performance from weaker whole-training averages. Its preference for final performance is a new evaluative qualification. The earlier Atari entropy explanation and proposed RLHF application remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 and Table 4 document the new MuJoCo experiments' optimizer, budgets, batch sizes, loss coefficients, and KL thresholds. Existing Atari settings and network structures are retained, with the architecture diagram moved into the main text. Code-access information remains equivalent; the unfilled checklist supplies no additional technical disclosures.

R1.justification: v5 adds the Todorov, Erez, and Tassa MuJoCo reference to support the continuous-control evaluation. The existing PPO, trust-region, and RLHF positioning remains essentially unchanged. Switching from author-year citations to numbered references does not change the cited research.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v5 enumerates the experimental overview, streamlines some notation and wording, moves sensitivity analysis from Section 4.4 to Appendix B.7, and consolidates appendix material. It also appends an unfilled NeurIPS checklist, without extensively rewriting the scientific narrative.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout, substantially rearranges plot grids and main-versus-appendix panels, adds legends, and moves the architecture diagram into the main text. New MuJoCo figures and tables are added. The over-optimization figure loses Riverraid and uses tighter KL axes that clip portions of the PPO curves.

improvement.justification: The six-task MuJoCo evaluation, Gaussian KL derivation, and documented settings strengthen evidence for applicability beyond Atari. Separating final-window and whole-training returns makes performance tradeoffs clearer. These gains are partly offset by removed stress-test evidence, clipped PPO curves in Figure 3, and an unfilled checklist. The net improvement is useful but limited.
